mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in CPIAUCSL, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher policy rates reduce discounting of future earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS month-over-month increase > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL month-over-month decrease > 0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: Rising inflation and tightening monetary policy cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during qualifying FEDFUNDS/CPIAUCSL moves (p > 0.05), or the interaction coefficient in a regression is positive and significant.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive 60-day forward returns as markets anticipate a prolonged accommodative stance.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative during all qualifying FEDFUNDS > 4% periods (p > 0.05), or the IC for the window is below -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) above the 50th percentile of its 12-month rolling distribution predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as strong job creation raises wage growth expectations and inflation pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month increase > +3.0% above prior month's 12-month median
regime_hint: Labor market tightening before wage growth peak
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive during all qualifying PAYEMS moves (p > 0.05), or the IC is positive and significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both HOUST (residential construction) and INDPRO (industrial production) for two consecutive months signals a demand softening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month decline > -5% AND INDPRO month-over-month decline > -4% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual output contraction in a growth cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such dual-output declines (p > 0.05), or interaction coefficient is non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO followed by a sustained rise in GDPC1 (personal consumption expenditures) for three consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as it signals a shift from contraction to recovery in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline > -6% for two months, then GDPC1 month-over-month increase > +2% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Transition from contraction to expansion in supply-side indicators
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative during the qualifying INDPRO/GDPC1 pattern (p > 0.05), or the interaction coefficient is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to show positive 20-day forward returns as lower unemployment expectations reduce risk premia.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month decrease < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying UNRATE declines (p > 0.05), or the IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -1% for four consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month decline < -1.0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during qualifying RSAFS declines (p > 0.05), or the IC is positive and significant.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in HOUST and PAYEMS above their respective 12-month medians for two consecutive months predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as strong housing and labor demand suggest economic acceleration.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month increase > +2% AND PAYEMS month-over-month increase > +1.5% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual demand acceleration in a recovery phase
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying HOUST/PAYEMS moves (p > 0.05), or the interaction coefficient is not statistically significant.
